$comment: npm-audit equivalent of .trivyignore, consumed by scripts/npm-audit-gate.mjs (the blocking Security Scan step). Every entry needs an advisory id, the tree it applies to (scope = npm prefix, or '*'), a reason, an added date, and an expires date. 🔴 expires is ENFORCED as of 2026-08-28: past its date the entry stops suppressing and the advisory blocks again, because a review cadence written only in prose is how a suppression list becomes permanent. Expiring does not mean the advisory is fixed — it means a human undertook to look again by then. Re-justify with a new date, or remove the entry.

exceptions.reason: image-size ICNS-parser DoS. npm reports the vulnerable range as '*' — EVERY published version is affected, so there is no version to upgrade to (1.2.1 is the last of the 1.x line, published the same day upstream moved to 2.0.2, and 2.x is not fixed either). npm's only offered 'fix' is react-native 0.72.17, flagged isSemVerMajor — a major DOWNGRADE from 0.81.5 that would break the app without fixing the flaw. Reachable only via metro, the Expo/React-Native dev bundler (@expo/metro, @react-native/community-cli-plugin): it reads image dimensions while building the JS bundle on a developer machine or CI runner, does not ship in the compiled APK/IPA, and never runs on a server. The images it parses are the repo's own committed assets, not untrusted input. Same reachability class as the undici/ws and image-size CVE entries in .trivyignore. Remove as soon as upstream publishes a fixed image-size that metro accepts.

image-size JXL/HEIF-parser DoS — same package, same vulnerable range '*', same dev-bundler-only reachability and same absent fix as GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr above; see that entry for the full reasoning. Remove both together when a fixed image-size ships.

node-forge RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification accepts extra nested DigestAlgorithm elements (CVE-2026-85393). Affected range <= 1.4.0, first_patched_version NONE, and 1.4.0 is the latest release, so there is no version to upgrade to. Reachable only through developer tooling: @expo/cli (src/utils/codesigning.js, src/run/ios/codeSigning/Security.js) and expo-updates' `codesigning:*` CLI (cli/build/*CodeSigningAsync.js) — expo-updates' runtime entry build/index.js does not import it, no mobile app source imports node-forge or @expo/code-signing-certificates, and app.json configures no update code signing, so nothing in the shipped APK/IPA verifies a signature with it. Short expiry on purpose: re-check for a fixed node-forge then. Mirrored in .trivyignore. Re-reviewed 2026-10-25: node-forge 1.4.0 is still the latest release (no fix published); no mobile app source imports node-forge or @expo/code-signing-certificates; app.json still configures no update code signing (updates.codeSigningCertificate absent); npm still offers only expo 54.0.38, a major downgrade.

zod memory exhaustion while validating oversized constrained collections (CVE-2023-54404). Affected range is everything below 4.6.6, so the 3.x line has no fix: 3.25.76 is the last 3.x release. The app's own zod is ^4.6.7 (fixed, E-113). The flagged copy is mobile/node_modules/@expo/cli/node_modules/zod@3.25.76, which @expo/cli pins at ^3.25.76 (still so in the latest @expo/cli, 58.1.15) and uses only in its dev server (DevToolsPlugin.schema.js, createMCPDevToolsExtensionSchema.js) on a developer machine: not in the app bundle, not on any server, never sees member input. npm's only offered fix is expo 54.0.38, a major DOWNGRADE. Forcing zod 4 into @expo/cli would change the API it was written against. Same decision and reasoning as the CVE-2023-54404 entry in .trivyignore (E-113, 24 Oct 2026), which covered only the Trivy gate; this is the matching npm-audit entry it missed. Remove when Expo moves @expo/cli to zod 4.
